maria_support: Morning — Acme reported a spike of 429s overnight around 02:00 UTC. Their logs show 'burst credits exhausted'. Any quick triage steps?

 tom_engineer: Can you paste the error payload and any rate-limit headers they saw?

 acme_sre: here's the error we captured from our app: ```json
{"error":"RateLimitError","message":"burst credits exhausted","status":429}
```
We also saw headers: `x-rate-limit-limit: 1200`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 16400`, `x-burst-credits-remaining: 0`.

 maria_support: thanks — are they using batched embeddings or many small requests? what pattern?

 acme_sre: nightly population job runs ~1200 concurrent embedding calls over 3 minutes to re-index docs.

 tom_engineer: that's the issue — the burst pool is getting drained. We have smoothing policies; by default short spikes use burst credits for up to 60s window. Their job is longer so credits ran out.

 sara_product: did they have burst_smoothing enabled or a reserved quota? If not, recommend pacing or reserving dedicated capacity for that job.

 maria_support: suggested repro steps to customer:
1) run a small script that mimics their job: `for i in {1..1200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"text"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings & done`
2) measure `x-burst-credits-remaining` header and watch for 429s
3) try `--max-concurrency 50` and see if it completes without 429s.

 tom_engineer: internal note — add an automatic alert when burst credits < 10% for orgs running > 500rps sustained for > 30s. Filed RFC-487.

 ingest_bot: deploy succeeded: batch-rate-limiter v1.2.0 => should help pacing for self-managed scripts.

 maria_support: I'll follow up with Acme and propose two options: 1) smooth the job (client-side rate limit/concurrency) 2) reserve dedicated capacity or schedule the job to spread across longer window. Also ask them to include SDK retry with exponential backoff on 429s.

 acme_sre: thanks, we'll try throttling to 50 concurrent and report back :thumbsup:
